scope: Fixed before first implementation and before any business runtime. Implementation of original PROTOCOL common-cause matching, no changed quality thresholds.
product_defect: Two independent closed panels agree an original contract contradiction is a product cause, grounded in exact source/native/image evidence. A strict numeric alarm alone is not a product defect. Count platform-specific common causes once across states/input routes; distinct platform code may require independent fixes.
residual_and_regression: Independent arm-blind common-cause adjudicator sees initial identity and anonymous final capsules only after both quality panels seal. Match agreed source/obligation/cause manifestations across versions. A base cause persisting is residual; a new confirmed final cause is regression. Preserve disagreements/uncertain cause separately.
claims: Only after quality panels seal, compare original participant product claims against confirmed causes. Strip condition labels; retain original evidence. Do not infer detecting a defect merely from receiving an automatic alarm. Distinguish alarm FDR and participant claim FDR; classic FPR N/A without a true-negative population.
success: Full fresh public actuals plus complete mandatory source audit, independent public/hidden required checks and no residual/regression; strict F or U blocks. Source-only API/style checks never become computed-runtime proof.
cost: Observed author wall + shared D0 native wall + each handoff through mandatory final image/source actuals endpoint, including queues and integration review work. Common design/host/engineering, external grading/publication/CI separate. Zero accepted PR denominator yields N/A successful delivery cost. Never drop failed arms from endpoint cost table.
no_adaptive_product_change: Do not alter natural initial or final sources after seals, do not inject defects, do not change expectations or generic tools after release. Any operator repair requires new attempt record and scope attribution. No task replacement after seeing outputs.
